description: Scroll in a direction, or toward the top/bottom edge of scrollable content. The until input scrolls to an off-screen selector in one command. refresh is pull-to-refresh: one slow pull down, refused with scroll_refresh_not_at_top while content is hidden above. The optional amount is the finger-path fraction of the viewport axis, honored up to 0.8 of it; directional scrolls reduce release momentum, while app scroll physics determine the final content offset. A visible keyboard shortens the swiped band instead of being dismissed; when too little is left, the command refuses with scroll_keyboard_occludes_surface. A directional scroll also reports the movement it observed as movement: moved, at-edge, unchanged, or unobserved when the two reads could not back a claim either way; an unchanged surface inside a container that still hides content in that direction refuses with scroll_no_progress rather than repeating the requested distance. The movement field is absent where a tier verifies per pass (top/bottom, until), where the runtime cannot read a screen, where a settle observation or a replay already owns that observation, or where the operator opted out of it. Times out after 90s; a caller-supplied budget extends it.

device.description: Device name; ids go in udid or serial.

durationMs.description: Scroll duration in milliseconds when the backend supports pacing.

maxPasses.description: Maximum scroll gestures for an until search (default 12). Requires until.

serial.description: Android, HarmonyOS, or Vega VVD serial.

settle.description: Once the UI goes quiet, return the diff vs the pre-action tree. Best-effort; never fails the action.

settleQuietMs.description: Settle: quiet window in ms (default 500, 300 on iOS simulator; broad iOS screen swaps hold at least 1500).

until.description: Repeat scroll passes until this selector is visible on screen, then stop. Not valid with the top/bottom edge directions, which carry their own stop condition.

name: scroll
title: Scroll in a direction or to an edge
